propositions: Add an mcp autodeploy target that implements blue-green container deployment with atomic nginx upstream pointer swap, building immutable compose-mcp:<sha> images and starting new containers on free A/B host ports (8092 or 8093) instead of colliding with compose-managed 8091.

Memory pre-check aborts mcp deployment if MemAvailable < MCP_MEM_MIN_MB (default 1024) before starting a second container, emitting AUTODEPLOY_MCP_MEM_ABORT marker and backing off without advancing deployed-sha.

Health-check the new container's /health endpoint within MCP_HEALTH_TIMEOUT (default 120s); if it fails, docker rm the new container, leave the old include unchanged, emit AUTODEPLOY_ERROR mcp-unhealthy, and exit with backoff.

Retire old mcp containers gracefully via docker stop --time 1260 (SIGTERM) to trigger the container's bounded self-drain (_mcp_health.run_http_with_grace), never docker rm -f, preserving in-flight certified operations while reaping exited containers and freeing A/B ports.

When managed mcp containers exceed MCP_RELEASES_CAP (default 3), emit AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP instead of forcing a kill, preventing port exhaustion and ensuring no collision when both A and B ports are bound by undrained containers.

Detect mcp-only changes via MCP_PATHS (src/rebar, Dockerfile.mcp, docker-compose.yml, uv.lock, pyproject.toml) to trigger mcp block independently; shared paths trigger both mcp and review-bot independently, and failure of mcp branch is fatal (blocks deployed-sha advance) with backoff retry.
